req.title: Login form GET
req.statement: The system shall serve a login form at GET /auth/login.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the login form should be served at the GET /auth/login endpoint. We need to ensure that this endpoint returns the correct HTTP status code and payload. The tests will cover positive, negative, and boundary cases to ensure robustness against common mutations.

tests.name: test_login_form_get_positive
preconditions: The Flask app is running in test mode.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/auth/login')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'<form' in r.data
assert b'name="username"' in r.data
assert b'name="password"' in r.data

tests.name: test_login_form_get_negative
preconditions: The Flask app is running in test mode.
actions: Send a POST request to /auth/login with invalid data.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'invalid', 'password': 'invalid'})
assert r.status_code == 405

tests.name: test_login_form_get_boundary
preconditions: The Flask app is running in test mode.
actions: Send a GET request to /auth/login with a very long URL.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()
long_url = '/auth/login' + '?' + 'a' * 2048
r = client.get(long_url)
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'<form' in r.data
assert b'name="username"' in r.data
assert b'name="password"' in r.data
